commit_message:
avfilter: add vif filter

This is Visual Information Fidelity (VIF) filter and one of the component
filters of VMAF. It outputs the average VIF score over all frames.

Signed-off-by: Ashish Singh <ashk43712@gmail.com>

index 9dfc0ec67f..426cb158da 100644

+++ b/doc/filters.texi
@@ -21264,10 +21264,31 @@ otherwise colors will be less saturated, more towards gray.
 
 @subsection Commands
 
 This filter supports the all above options as @ref{commands}.
 
+@section vif
+
+Obtain the average VIF (Visual Information Fidelity) between two input videos.
+
+This filter takes two input videos.
+
+Both input videos must have the same resolution and pixel format for
+this filter to work correctly. Also it assumes that both inputs
+have the same number of frames, which are compared one by one.
+
+The obtained average VIF score is printed through the logging system.
+
+The filter stores the calculated VIF score of each frame.
+
+In the below example the input file @file{main.mpg} being processed is compared
+with the reference file @file{ref.mpg}.
+
+@example
+ffmpeg -i main.mpg -i ref.mpg -lavfi vif -f null -
+@end example
+
 @anchor{vignette}
 @section vignette

fix_commit.message: avfilter/vf_vif: Fix out of array access with small dimensions
fix_commit.author: Jiale Yao

findings.title: Insufficient boundary mirroring causes out-of-bounds array access with small image dimensions
findings.message: In vif_filter1d(), when computing the vertical and horizontal 1D filter passes near image edges, out-of-range indices ii/jj are 'mirrored' back into range using a single-step reflection: `ii = ii < 0 ? -ii : (ii >= h ? 2*h - ii - 1 : ii)` (and analogously for jj/w). This single reflection only corrects an index that is out of range by up to h (or w) once. Because the filter half-width is filt_w/2 == 8, an index can be out of range by more than the image dimension when h or w is smaller than filt_w/2 (e.g. a 1x1 input). In that case a single reflection does not bring the index back into [0, h-1] (or [0, w-1]); the resulting ii/jj can still be negative or >= h/w (e.g. reaching 8 or -7 for h=w=1), causing src[ii*src_stride+j] and temp[jj] to be read out of bounds, leading to an out-of-bounds heap read / undefined behavior.
findings.suggestion: Replace the hand-rolled single-step reflection with a proper repeated mirroring function such as FFmpeg's avpriv_mirror(), which repeatedly folds the index back into range and is correct regardless of how small the dimension is relative to the filter width. E.g. `ii = avpriv_mirror(ii, h - 1);` and `jj = avpriv_mirror(jj, w - 1);`. Include libavutil/internal.h for avpriv_mirror().

ground_truth.root_cause: The mirroring/reflection logic used to clamp filter indices near image boundaries was implemented as a single conditional reflection (`ii < 0 ? -ii : ...`) rather than a proper repeated/folded mirroring, which is only valid when the amount of overshoot does not exceed the array dimension itself. Small image dimensions (smaller than filt_w/2) violate this assumption, allowing indices computed as `i - filt_w/2 + filt_i` to overshoot by more than h or w, producing indices still out of the valid [0, dim-1] range after one reflection.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Insufficient boundary mirroring causes out-of-bounds array access with small image dimensions
